title: Closed-point local structure and differential rank on a smooth integral curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a separated integral scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension one [def-pc-curve], smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $x\in X$ be a closed point. Put $A=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, with its $k$-algebra structure induced by the structure morphism. Then $\dim A=1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], and every open neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ has topological Krull dimension $1$, so $\dim_xX=1$ [def-kun-dimension]. The ring $A$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], hence Noetherian, and is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. The module of Kähler differentials $\Omega_{A/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] is free of rank one: there exists an $A$-linear isomorphism $A\xrightarrow{\sim}\Omega_{A/k}$. No separability assumption on $\kappa(x)/k$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0C1E, lemma-uniformizer-works, first and last proof sentences: the DVR assertion and rank-one differential module; old Steps 1–3 of lem-a1-uniformizer-differential-basis, including both dimension conventions

proof.text: By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], the dimension-one hypothesis in [def-pc-curve] gives topological Krull dimension $\dim X=1$. Integrality makes $X$ irreducible and nonempty by [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible]. Apply [lem-sc-scheme-sober] to the irreducible closed subset $X$ to obtain a generic point $\eta$, with $\overline{\{\eta\}}=X$. We have $\eta\ne x$: otherwise closedness of $x$ gives $X=\{x\}$, whose only nonempty irreducible closed subset is itself, so its dimension is zero, a contradiction.

source.place: Tags 04MU (lemma-dimension), 01ON (lemma-characterize-integral); Schemes Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); dimension clarification for Curves Tag 0C1E (lemma-uniformizer-works)

proof.text: Since $x\in\overline{\{\eta\}}$ and $x\ne\eta$, the chain $x,\eta$ has length one. By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], $\dim A\geq1$; by [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], $\dim A\leq\dim X=1$. Thus $\dim A=1$. For any open neighbourhood $N$ of $x$, $\eta\in N$ (otherwise the closed complement of $N$ contains $\eta$ and hence $X$). Its closure in $N$ is $N$, so $N$ is irreducible. The strict chain $\{x\}\subsetneq N$ of nonempty irreducible closed subsets of $N$ gives $\dim N\geq1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-subspace-dimension-monotone], $\dim N\leq\dim X=1$. Every such $N$ therefore has dimension one, and [def-kun-dimension] gives $\dim_xX=1$.

source.place: Tag 02IZ (lemma-codimension-local-ring), Tag 04MU (lemma-dimension); Topology Tag 0055 (definition-Krull) and following open-subspace remark

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$, and let $\mathfrak q$ represent $x$. The restriction $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Hence $B$ is a smooth $k$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine]. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local], $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local. The $k$-algebra identification $A\cong B_{\mathfrak q}$ supplied by the germ localization in [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] makes $A$ regular local, hence Noetherian by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Its dimension is one by step 2, so [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] makes it a discrete valuation ring.

source.place: Tag 00TT (lemma-characterize-smooth-over-field), final assertion; Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), regular dimension-one case; Morphisms Tag 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize); Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves)

proof.text: For the structure morphism $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, the fibre over the unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is $X$: the residue field there is $k$, so the fibre is $X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}k$ with the identity as second map. Thus its dimension at $x$ is one by step 2. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-differentials-free-rank-fibre-dimension] to obtain an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$ of $x$ with $\Omega_{C/k}=Ce$ freely on one generator $e$. Here the target affine neighbourhood is necessarily all of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\mathfrak p$ represent $x$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $A\cong C_{\mathfrak p}$ as $k$-algebras. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization], $\Omega_{A/k}\cong(\Omega_{C/k})_{\mathfrak p}$. The isomorphism $C_{\mathfrak p}\to(Ce)_{\mathfrak p}$ sends $c/s$ to $ce/s$; its inverse sends $ce/s$ to $c/s$. These formulas are well-defined because equality of module fractions is the same equality of coefficients in the free basis $e$. Composing gives an $A$-linear isomorphism $A\cong\Omega_{A/k}$. All these maps use the original structure map $k\to A$; no condition on $\kappa(x)/k$ has been used.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_curve_closed_stalk_structure (k : Type u) [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsIntegralCurve f] [Smooth f] (x : X) (hx : IsClosed ({x} : Set X)) : ringKrullDim (X.presheaf.stalk x) = 1 ∧ (∀ N : X.Opens, x ∈ N → topologicalKrullDim N = 1) ∧ topologicalKrullDimAt x = 1 ∧ IsRegularLocalRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsNoetherianRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ IsDiscreteValuationRing (X.presheaf.stalk x) ∧ Nonempty ((X.presheaf.stalk x) ≃ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x] @KaehlerDifferential k (X.presheaf.stalk x) _ _ (((Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of k)).inv ≫ f.appTop ≫ X.presheaf.germ ⊤ x trivial).hom.toAlgebra))
